name: census-acs
description: U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) data, used to back a grant narrative's community-need statement with real Hispanic/Latino population, poverty, and demographic figures for the org's service area. Read-only, no relationship to funder matching.

auth.type: API key as a URL query parameter (key=...)
auth.note: This plugin ships with a placeholder, not a real key — each installer must get their own free key (instant, no OAuth) at https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html and paste it in here. Do not use a shared/personal key here if this plugin is ever distributed to others.

critical_bug.summary: WebFetch reliably returns EMPTY for any Census API URL combining a SPECIFIC for= value (e.g. for=county:201) with an in= clause (e.g. in=state:39) — confirmed via repeated testing, even though the identical URL returns correct data in a browser or via curl with a normal User-Agent. A wildcard for= value combined with in= (e.g. for=place:*&in=state:48) works fine; it's specifically the for=<type>:<specific-code>&in=state:<code> combination that fails.
critical_bug.rule: NEVER construct a query of the form for=<type>:<specific-code>&in=state:<code> for the actual data fetch. Always use the ucgid= parameter instead (see workflow below) to target one specific geography — this has been tested and works reliably. Wildcard for= queries (no in=, or wildcard for= with in=) are fine for the geography-lookup step.

step_1_resolve_geography.description: Find the FIPS code(s) for the org's city or county by name. Do this once per org location, not per query.

county_lookup.notes: Fetches all ~3,143 US counties in one call (large response, but confirmed working via WebFetch). Search the returned rows for a name match like 'Harris County, Texas'; the row includes the state and county FIPS codes.

place_lookup.notes: Fetches all incorporated places within one state — needs the state FIPS code first (a stable, small lookup you can reason about directly, e.g. Texas=48, Ohio=39, California=06). This is a wildcard for= with in=, which works fine — only a SPECIFIC for= value with in= is broken (see critical_bug).

step_2_construct_ucgid.description: Build a single ucgid string from the FIPS code(s) found in step 1 — this is what step 3 actually queries with.

step_3_fetch_data.notes: Use the most recent year with data available (ACS 5-year estimates lag ~1-2 years behind the current date). Always use ucgid here, never for=<specific>&in=.

key_variables.B03001_003E: Hispanic or Latino population (aggregate, all origins)
key_variables.B17001_001E: Total population for whom poverty status is determined
key_variables.B17001_002E: Population with income below the poverty level in the past 12 months

usage_notes: ACS 5-year estimates are the most reliable for small geographies (city/county level) — 1-year estimates only exist for large areas (~65k+ population) and can be noisier.
Compute percentages yourself from the raw counts (e.g. Hispanic/Latino share = B03001_003E / B03001_001E) — the API returns raw totals, not percentages.
This connector is for community-need context in a grant narrative, not for funder matching — keep it a separate, clearly-labeled section in the skill's output, not mixed into the ranked funder table.
